page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-30 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 30 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 15 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, running two threads per core. The instance configuration allocates 59.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.97 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for advanced vector instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic hardware acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance contains no bundled local storage and does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU throughput testing in the top 25 percent at 2865.07. Multithreaded execution aligns with mid-tier industry baselines, producing a stress-ng multi-core score of 43031.83 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 14394.0. Text processing capabilities and PassMark memory metrics also perform in the upper quartile. However, the platform exhibits an operational tradeoff in sustained uncached write bandwidth, recording 25.11 GB/sec in 256MB write block tests, placing it in the lower 25 percent. Read-intensive memory operations maintain standard throughput, registering 72.56 GB/sec in large block tests and 2124.95 GB/sec in cached 16KB operations.

Given its compute-heavy memory-to-core ratio and dedicated AMD EPYC resources, this instance profile is tailored for compute-bound operations that require high per-thread efficiency without excessive RAM footprints. Typical deployment environments include continuous integration and compilation pipelines, batch text processing, microservices, and lightweight CPU-based inference workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-30 is a compute-focused instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It features 30 dedicated vCPUs across 15 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, alongside 59.0 GB of memory (1.97 GB per vCPU). The instance includes AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets, but includes no local storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU execution (stress-ng score of 2865.07) and upper-quartile memory responsiveness, alongside solid results in text processing and lightweight language model inference. Multithreaded throughput and uncached read bandwidth align with average mid-tier standards, while uncached memory write throughput registers in the lower quartile. The configuration suits CPU-intensive workloads such as build pipelines, web serving, and analytical text processing.
